A courier guild carries sealed letters across a salt desert between rival cities. Reader promise: slow-burn travel adventure with a guild intrigue underneath.

# Voice sheet

## Narration contract

Viewpoint Sena: third person limited, past tense, close distance. No head-hopping inside a scene.

## Tone palette

Baseline: dry, observant, unhurried. Permitted excursion: gallows humour under physical danger, returning to baseline by the end of the scene. Excluded: slapstick, narrator sentimentality.

## Language conventions

British spelling. Guild ranks are lower-case. No modern idiom in dialogue.

## Anchor passages

- ch-003, revision r4: the night crossing, from "The salt sang under her boots" to the scene break.
- ch-008, revision r2: the ledger argument with Oren, whole scene.

## Deliberate exceptions

ch-009 uses present tense for the fever dream.

## Change log

- V1 accepted by the author after the voice trial.

# World overview

The salt-road courier guild has three ranks. A runner carries unsealed post inside one city. A courier carries sealed letters between cities and may refuse a commission. A warden keeps a gate ledger and settles disputes between couriers and clients.

The Brine Gate had closed its ledger before Sena reached it. She read her own name there, entered in a hand that was not hers, and went round by the tannery stair.

Oren was waiting where the vats ended. He held out the letter, seal unbroken, and she saw that the wax was the wrong red.
